---
title: "easyQDA-quarto-theme"
---


A Quarto website theme with one distinctive property: the built site
keeps working when it is opened from a plain file tree — `file://`, or
the `chrome://` address of help bundled into a Zotero plugin. Search,
math, the table of contents that follows the scroll, the dark-mode
toggle: all of it, with **no request ever leaving the page**. Fonts and
MathJax ship with the site.

The look is what you are reading right now: a centred three-column
layout with a frosted-glass header, self-hosted Noto Sans, quiet
sidebars with a soft accent pill on the current page, and Quarto's
native callouts, in light and dark. This documentation is built with
the theme it documents — every claim on these pages is tested by the
page you see it on.

The theme was built for the [zotQDA](https://zotqda.org) documentation
sites — [qdaPy](https://qdapy.zotqda.org) and
[qdaR](https://qdar.zotqda.org) use it, and this site does too. It is
generic enough for any documentation site with the same needs.

```sh
quarto add easyqda/easyQDA-quarto-theme
```

```yaml
format:
  zotqda-theme-html: default
```

## What the theme does not do

It does not try to style arbitrary Quarto documents — it is a website
theme, written against the HTML that Quarto's website projects produce.
And it does not promise that any Quarto version will do: both the
styling rules and the offline repairs are written against a pinned
version, and the pin moves deliberately, with a test, not silently.
